text:
Zoe (Product Designer): Quick design check — I'm proposing a small restructure for the on‑prem preflight step: show the CIDR input and detection results side-by-side, move the 'what we check' accordion below, and tone down the scanner copy. Sketch in thread.
Mike (PM): Sketch? link pls. main goal is reduce support tickets for common misconfigs.
Zoe (Product Designer): https://figma.com/file/x123 — page 'preflight v3'. Main intent: make failures actionable. Eg instead of 'Connection failed' -> 'Agent couldn't reach 10.0.0.0/24 on port 443. Check firewall and route from host to internet.'
Eve (UX Writer): Love the actionable focus. Alternate microcopy for failures: 1) "Agent couldn't reach the control plane at <ip>. Verify firewall egress and NAT." 2) "No route to <ip>: check VPC route table and host routing." Thoughts on tone?
Mike (PM): Keep it direct, not scary. Prefer the first one but remove jargon like NAT for customers who might be infra beginners.
Sanjay (Eng - Runtime): Quick technical note: the on‑prem agent cannot reliably probe arbitrary ports on remote infra due to customer security zones. We detect reachability from agent to our control plane TLS endpoint and fall back to DNS-level checks. So microcopy mustn't imply we scanned internal ports. Eg don't say 'scanned port 443' — instead 'couldn't establish a TLS connection to <host>'.
Eve (UX Writer): Good catch. Revised fail example: "Agent couldn't establish a secure connection to <host>:443. Ensure outbound TLS egress to that host is allowed." Cleaner?
Alana (Accessibility): A couple of a11y nits: 1) The CIDR input needs proper aria-describedby linking to the helper text that explains allowed formats. 2) The scanner status should not rely on color alone — include icons + text. 3) If we render the accordion, ensure keyboard focus order follows visual flow.
Zoe (Product Designer): Agreed on all. For the side-by-side layout I can ensure the status has icon + sr-only text + visible caption. Also adding a small helper link "What we test" that expands inline is better for keyboard users than a big accordion.
Sanjay (Eng - Runtime): Also performance note: live scanning each time will slow down the flow. Let's cache last successful preflight for 10 minutes and show a warning badge "Last checked 3m ago" with an option to re-run. That avoids blocking users during quick retries.
Mike (PM): Nice. That also reduces noisy backend calls. Can we show estimated scan time so users know when to expect the result?
Sanjay (Eng - Runtime): We can expose a progress state: queued -> probing -> done/failed. Probing duration varies but typically <7s. I'll add telemetry to surface median times by region.
Eve (UX Writer): Adding inline microcopy suggestions: - Idle: "Preflight will check connectivity and required ports — this usually takes <10s." - Running: "Checking..." with spinner and ETA if >3s. - Success: "All checks passed." - Partial fail: "Some checks failed — expand for details and remediation steps"
Alana (Accessibility): For ETA, ensure it's an estimate, not a live countdown. Screen readers should announce status changes; use polite live region for updates.
Zoe (Product Designer): I'll update the mock with the new phrasing + a11y annotations and push an updated frame in 30m. Can folks review before EOD?
Mike (PM): I’ll review, esp. the remediation steps copy for support friendliness.
Sanjay (Eng - Runtime): I'll sanity-check tokens/requests used by the preflight to ensure we don't expose any extra customer info.
Eve (UX Writer): Ping me if you want alternate microcopy for the 'Last checked' badge.
deploy-bot: Documentation link updated: https://docs.redwood.ai/onprem/preflight
Zoe (Product Designer): Thanks all — will post the updated frame here. :thumbsup:
